_about: Public-domain George Burder (1752-1832), Congregationalist minister of Fetter Lane, London, a founder of the London Missionary Society and the Religious Tract Society, for the Word Hoard: Evangelical Truth Defended (1788) and Village Sermons (1798), from Internet Archive scans of Eighteenth Century Collections. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 49 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

burder-evangelical-truth: Evangelical truth defended: or, a reply to a letter, containing strictures on a sermon, preached at Lancaster, by the Rev. Mr. Housman. ... By George Burder.  1788 (catalogued 1788)
burder-village-sermons: Village sermons; or, twelve plain and short discourses on the principal doctrines of the Gospel; intended for the use of families, Sunday-schools, or companies ... Volume I. Third edition revised. By George Burder.  1798 (catalogued 1798)

_alternates.burder-copies: Later printings of The Good Old Way (1783-1792) and Village Sermons (1798-1799)

_excluded.burder-other: His 1797 single-sermon tracts; the Welsh Village Sermons (1799); The Welch Indians (1797, a compilation)

_pending.burder-early-piety: Early Piety, or Memoirs of Children eminently serious (2nd ed., London: H. Trapp, 1777): the title page, read from the page image, names no author ('Recommended by the Rev. Mr. Peckwell'); attributed to Burder by the catalogue only
